name: ARX-related Epileptic Encephalopathy

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in the ARX gene
Onset of refractory seizures within the first 6 months of life
Severe global developmental delay or regression following seizure onset
EEG showing burst suppression or hypsarrhythmia pattern
Presence of structural brain abnormalities such as agenesis of the corpus callosum

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic ARX gene variant plus early-onset refractory seizures and severe developmental delay
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing; clinical features and EEG support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Seizures typically begin within the first 6 months of life
Profound cognitive impairment following seizure onset

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplasia or agenesis of the corpus callosum

common.notes: Head circumference below normal for age

common.symptomName: Abnormal EEG patterns (burst suppression or hypsarrhythmia)
common.notes: Typical EEG abnormalities in epileptic encephalopathy
searchTerms: burst suppression or chaotic brain activity

occasional.notes: Involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal postures

occasional.symptomName: Visual impairment due to optic nerve hypoplasia
occasional.notes: Reduced vision related to optic nerve abnormalities
searchTerms: poor vision from small optic nerves
optic nerve underdevelopment causing vision loss
vision problems due to optic nerve issues

occasional.notes: Common in infants with feeding difficulties

rare.notes: Spinal curvature developing in later infancy
Secondary to hypotonia and aspiration risk

laboratory: Possible metabolic screening abnormalities secondary to seizures
imaging: MRI showing agenesis or hypoplasia of corpus callosum
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ARX gene (X-linked inheritance)
other: EEG with burst suppression or hypsarrhythmia pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic triad of infantile spasms, developmental regression, and hypsarrhythmia
Multiple genetic causes other than ARX

redFlags: Onset of refractory seizures within first 6 months of life
Severe global developmental delay or regression
Identification of pathogenic ARX gene variant
references: Kato M, et al. ARX mutations and early infantile epileptic encephalopathy. Epilepsia. 2011.
Shoubridge C, et al. ARX spectrum disorders: genotype-phenotype correlations and molecular mechanisms. Hum Mutat. 2010.
